front: What is Compile time in one sentence?
back: Phase before program runs — parsing, type checking, optimization, and codegen; errors here prevent broken binaries from shipping.

front: Explain the mental model of Compile time (how the system thinks).
back: Compile time = while compiler/transpiler/build tool runs. Runtime = while program executes. Decisions at compile time are fixed (types, const generics, #ifdef); runtime handles user input, network, dynamic dispatch (virtual methods, interface{}, reflection).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Compile time?
back: tsc --noEmit → go build ./... → cargo check # fast typecheck → cargo clippy # lints

front: Given a broken Compile time setup, what is your first validation command?
back: tsc --noEmit

front: Symptom: Build fails CI, passes locally — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Toolchain version · Fix: Pin Node/Go/Rust in CI

front: Symptom: Slow builds — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Incremental broken · Fix: Cache artifacts; split modules

front: Symptom: Type error cascade — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: One root error · Fix: Fix first error; rerun

front: Symptom: #ifdef wrong branch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: -D flags · Fix: Align Makefile/CMake defines

front: Symptom: Works in IDE, fails tsc — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: stricter CI tsconfig · Fix: Align strict flags

front: Gotcha with Compile time: what silently fails?
back: Template/macro errors — line numbers lie; preprocessed output helps (gcc -E). Conditional compilation drift — prod build missing FEATURE_X silently. Transpiler ≠ typecheck — Babel alone doesn't typecheck TypeScript.

front: When should you NOT use Compile time?
back: Don't push runtime validation-only languages to "compile time" metaphors without static checker (add TypeScript/mypy). Don't over-use macros/templates — debug at compile time becomes nightmare.

front: What is Compiler in one sentence?
back: Translates source in a high-level language to machine code or bytecode for a target platform — portability via abstraction over CPU ISAs.

front: Explain the mental model of Compiler (how the system thinks).
back: Source → frontend (parse, AST) → optimizer → backend (codegen for x86/ARM/WASM). Different hardware (x86, ARM, RISC-V) needs different instruction streams; compilers hide that. Interpreted languages still often compile to bytecode (JVM, CPython .pyc) — JIT bridges compile time and runtime.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Compiler?
back: source.c → compiler (clang) → object file → linker → executable → source.ts → tsc → JavaScript → (optional) V8 JIT → gcc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -c file.c -o file.o → gcc file.o -o app → clang -std=c17 -g -fsanitize=address file.c -o app_asan # debug memory

front: Given a broken Compiler setup, what is your first validation command?
back: source.c → compiler (clang) → object file → linker → executable

front: Symptom: Undefined reference — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Link stage · Fix: Add -l library; include .o

front: Symptom: Works on dev, SIGILL on prod — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CPU features · Fix: -march too new; build on oldest target

front: Symptom: Optimizer bug — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: -O0 vs -O2 · Fix: Bisect flags; UB in C (sanitizers)

front: Symptom: Wrong arch binary — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: file bin · Fix: Cross-compile GOOS/GOARCH or toolchain prefix

front: Symptom: Huge binary — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Debug symbols · Fix: strip or -s; split debug info

front: Gotcha with Compiler: what silently fails?
back: Undefined behavior in C — optimizer assumes rules; "works in debug" classic. Cross-compile needs sysroot/libs — not just compiler binary. Reproducible builds — timestamps and paths embed in binary unless -trimpath/SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

front: When should you NOT use Compiler?
back: Don't hand-write assembly for whole app unless extreme hot path — maintainability cost. Don't -O3 blindly on latency-sensitive code without profiling — can regress.

front: What is library file in one sentence?
back: Static (.a) vs shared (.so / .dylib / .dll) native libraries — how SEs link C/C++/Rust deps in CI and production.

front: Explain the mental model of library file (how the system thinks).
back: Linux loader: ld.so reads DT_NEEDED, searches LD_LIBRARY_PATH, /etc/ld.so.cache, RUNPATH/RPATH.

front: Symptom: error while loading shared libraries: libfoo.so — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ldd ./app in prod image · Fix: Install package; set RUNPATH; copy .so next to binary

front: Symptom: Wrong .so version loaded — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: LD_DEBUG=libs ./app · Fix: Align SONAME; remove stale paths from LD_LIBRARY_PATH

front: Symptom: Works locally, fails CI — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Dev machine has extra libs · Fix: Minimal container reproduce; explicit -L / vendoring

front: Symptom: undefined reference at link — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing -l or wrong order · Fix: Put -lfoo after objects that use it

front: Symptom: GLIBCXX_3.4.xx not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: libstdc++ mismatch · Fix: Match build/runtime GCC; use same base image

front: Symptom: Static binary huge / NSS issues — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: glibc static quirks · Fix: Prefer shared linking on Linux services

front: Gotcha with library file: what silently fails?
back: Mixing static and shared for same lib (e.g. OpenSSL) — symbol duplication / ODR violations → subtle crashes.

front: When should you NOT use library file?
back: Pure managed runtimes (JVM, Node, Python wheels) — use package manager / manylinux wheels unless writing native extensions. Static everything on glibc Linux servers — ops and security updates harder; shared distro libs preferred. Vendor .so without ABI pin — upgrade host OS breaks app; containerize or bundle exact SONAME.

front: What is Transpiler in one sentence?
back: Source-to-source translator — modern syntax down-levelled for older runtimes; runs at build time, not in user's browser (usually).

front: Explain the mental model of Transpiler (how the system thinks).
back: A compiler often targets machine code/bytecode; a transpiler targets another high-level language (TS→JS, ES2022→ES5). Developer runs it locally or in CI; deploy artifact is the output. Bundlers (Webpack, esbuild, Vite) chain transpile + bundle + minify.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Transpiler?
back: author TS/JSX → Babel/SWC/tsc → deploy JS → browser/V8 → npm i -D @babel/core @babel/preset-env @babel/preset-typescript

front: Given a broken Transpiler setup, what is your first validation command?
back: author TS/JSX → Babel/SWC/tsc → deploy JS → browser/V8

front: Symptom: Syntax error in old browser — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Build target · Fix: Lower @babel/preset-env targets

front: Symptom: Missing polyfill — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: core-js · Fix: useBuiltIns: 'usage' or manual import

front: Symptom: TS types ignored — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Using Babel only · Fix: Add tsc --noEmit or fork-ts-checker

front: Symptom: Huge bundle — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Full polyfill · Fix: Target modern browsers; analyze bundle

front: Symptom: Source maps wrong — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: devtool setting · Fix: source-map in prod selectively

front: Gotcha with Transpiler: what silently fails?
back: Ship transpiled code, not raw TS — Node still often runs TS via ts-node in dev only. Double transpile — Babel + tsc both transforming = slow/conflicts. Decorators/experimental — stage mismatches break silently across versions.

front: When should you NOT use Transpiler?
back: Don't transpile if targets are evergreen-only (internal tools) — ship native ES2022. Don't transpile on the server per request — always prebuild in CI.
